questions.question: What is the largest large-load figure, in MW, among the public large-load statements the warehouse holds for ERCOT's grid?
questions.answer: The largest large-load figure for ERCOT's grid is 474,000 MW (large_load_public, model-extracted). It comes from a statement dated 2026-07-29 (UTC), in the document "ERCOT Update, Texas Senate hearing of July 29, 2026, Panel 1: Assessing the Grid". The warehouse does not class this row by stage. I found the maximum over 55 ERCOT rows with row_kind mw, including the figures from ERCOT, Oncor and CenterPoint. The next-largest ERCOT figure is 445,800 MW, dated 2026-04-01. By source, the largest figure for Oncor Electric Delivery is 137,900 MW and for CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric 17,000 MW. These are aggregate figures from public statements. They are not single-customer loads.

questions.question: In Berkeley Lab's Queued Up data, how many MW of solar-only requests were active in PJM's queue at the end of 2025?
questions.answer: The Queued Up data (interconnection_queue_summary, derived from Berkeley Lab/GridTracker) shows 54,121.7 MW of solar-only requests active in PJM's queue (entity queue:pjm:solar, variable total_active_mw). That is 638 requests (total_active_requests). The table's newest row is labelled 1 January 2025 (UTC) and covers requests entered through 2025. The warehouse holds one file snapshot, not a dated 31 December 2025 balance, so I read this total as the end-of-2025 figure. Solar-plus-battery requests are a separate entity and are not included. A narrower figure is also held: 11,571.1 MW (mw_active) of active requests that entered the queue in 2025 alone.

questions.question: What was the median time from interconnection request to commercial operation for ERCOT projects that reached operation in 2025, in months?
questions.answer: The median time from interconnection request to commercial operation for ERCOT projects that reached operation in 2025 was 48.7 months (interconnection_durations_summary, variable median_months, row dated 2025-01-01, which is the 2025 year). That figure covers 69 completed projects totaling 9,006.27 MW. The interquartile range was 22.7 to 59.8 months. The table is derived from Berkeley Lab's Queued Up file.
